newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: LME tin seen rebounding, outlook uncertain - trade.
newsitem.headline: LME tin seen rebounding, outlook uncertain - trade.

text.p: Tin prices on the London Metal Exchange (LME) are expected to rebound on Tuesday as the sharp drop overnight was seen as overdone, Malaysian dealers and analysts said.
"The market was definitely oversold yesterday. The drop was not reflective of the market as volume was very thin," said an analyst at a major tin company.
He expects the market to stage a technical rebound on Tuesday. "The market should recover quite well," he said.

Three-month tin hit an 18-month low of $5,810 a tonne on Monday before ending the day at $5,840, a loss of $180 from Friday. Analysts pegged immediate support at $5,800 though a stronger base would be at $5,750, they said.
A Malaysian trader said tin could recover up to $100 on Tuesday. "The sharp fall overnight was not expected. It was overdone," he said.
Local traders added that they were not aware of any selling from Malaysia on the London market.

One analyst in London said that Chinese and Malaysian selling was at least partly behind the slide that began on Friday, as the two nations sought to take advantage of domestic export quotas before the year-end.
Analysts, however, were uncertain over the metal's near-term prospects, saying tin would remain vulnerable to developments elsewhere in the base metals complex, particularly copper.
"It's always difficult to predict where the tin market is heading, though we believe tin is undervalued at current prices," said another analyst.
Meanwhile, Malaysia's tin market showed a mild reaction to the drop in London. The price closed at 14.72 ringgit ($5.83) a kg on Tuesday, down 19 cents.
"The local market was reacting to the fall in LME but the drop here was not as bad as expected. I think market players are anticipating a sharp rebound in LME today," said one trader.
He said he was not alarmed by the slump in London prices as the local market had shown some independence.
Traders said that although further losses in London could weigh on the local price, strong support is expected at 14.50 ringgit.
